findings.one_line: The non-Gaussian expected-length decomposition omits the event φ_n=1 but I_D∩I_A=∅, on which C_n^*=I_D has length O(d_n); the slope event (11) and selector error do not control this intercept/calibration failure, whose fixed-α probability can yield an O(d_n) contribution and invalidate the claimed B_n/δ_n shortening.
Its conclusion L_N(C_n^*)=o(d_n) relies on the invalid non-Gaussian expected-length bound in thm:adaptive-upper-frontier; the unaccounted empty-intersection fallback can remain order d_n.

The asserted O(n^{-3/8}) non-Gaussian coordinate is obtained solely from the invalid shortening clause of thm:adaptive-upper-frontier; the stated construction has an unboundedly larger O(n^{-1/4}) fallback contribution under the reproduced decomposition.
